questions.prompt: Given two tables, Orders(order_id, customer_id) and Customers(customer_id, name), which SQL clause correctly returns only customers who have placed an order?

options.text: SELECT Customers.name FROM Customers INNER JOIN Orders ON Customers.customer_id = Orders.customer_id;
SELECT Customers.name FROM Customers LEFT JOIN Orders ON Customers.customer_id = Orders.customer_id;
SELECT Customers.name FROM Customers RIGHT JOIN Orders ON Customers.customer_id = Orders.customer_id;
SELECT Customers.name FROM Customers FULL JOIN Orders ON Customers.customer_id = Orders.customer_id;

questions.explanation: INNER JOIN returns rows that have matching keys in both tables.

questions.prompt: Which join type returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table, filling with NULL where no match exists?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows and adds NULLs for missing right rows.
